lost_facts.assertion: assert error.retained_prompt_tokens == 0  # AssertionError: assert -61 == 0, where -61 = ExampleTooLongError('example of 129 tokens exceeds max_seq_length=40: -61 prompt tokens would survive, minimum is 16').retained_prompt_tokens
lost_facts.evidence: The agent's own code (transcript line 4894) computes `retained_prompt_tokens = spans[-1][0] - window_start` and feeds it straight into ExampleTooLongError with no floor: `if window_start > 0 and spans: retained_prompt_tokens = spans[-1][0] - window_start; if retained_prompt_tokens < MIN_RETAINED_PROMPT_TOKENS: raise ExampleTooLongError(...)`. When the final assistant span starts well before the window (the TOO_LONG_PAIRS case: token_count 129, window_start 89, final span start 28), the raw subtraction is -61 rather than 0. The refusal itself still fires correctly (since -61 < 16), so the *behavior* (refuse, skip-and-count) is right, but the *attribute value* the error carries is wrong. The agent's own docstring for ExampleTooLongError (line 4579) frames retained_prompt_tokens as 'prompt tokens surviving in front of the final assistant turn' — a count that cannot logically be negative — yet the code never clamps it. No remark in the corpus states this floor explicitly (only window_start's own floor at 0 is stated, in page 153 / g9.r1.say27, a distinct quantity); the agent never reasoned about or tested this edge case — every self-authored test in tests/finetune/test_data_formatter.py that exercised ExampleTooLongError happened to produce retained_prompt_tokens == 0 or a small positive number (e.g. the 'example of 5 tokens exceeds max_seq_length=2: 0 prompt tokens would survive' case at line 5330), never a deeply negative one, so its own 133-test suite never caught the bug before push.

search_strategy: Systematic and unusually thorough for all four surfaces. Gitea issues were checked first and correctly ruled out as upstream noise (line 1120-1126). BookStack: keyword search first, then every hit fetched whole via a small helper script (pg.py) that pulls both page body and comments — it read 10 of the 15 wiki-comment carriers this way, but missed pages 135 and 154 because no search term it tried ('encoding','finetune','role sequence','formatter','validate','spans','tokenizer','EncodingReport','last_report','dropped_indices','FIREWORKS_BYTES_PER_TOKEN','653') happened to match them, and it never fell back to enumerating the whole Engineering collection — exactly the trap the ticket warns about (BookStack search does not index comments). Mattermost: got a session token, tried the /posts/search API first (thin, exact-phrase only), then pivoted to dumping five of six channels whole (engineering, code-review, releases, cookbooks, pipeline) to local files and grepping distinctive terms repeatedly and re-reading surrounding context with sed — but never dumped #viewer, missing its one remark (g9.r2.l9). Mail: dumped the entire IMAP mailbox to one file up front and grepped/sed'd through it systematically, covering nearly every relevant thread completely, including full multi-message threads. No truncation or crashed helper scripts hurt it; the '[horizon watchdog] terminal unchanged' nudges were consistently answered correctly with a fresh command rather than idle polling.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run succeeded end to end: implementation compiled, its own 133 added/modified tests passed, it was committed, pushed to main, CI reported success, and the release deployed (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1). Six of seven hidden facts scored 1; the sole 0 (g9.r1.failure_behavior) is a narrow implementation bug (missing max(0, ...) floor on retained_prompt_tokens), not a research or process failure.
notable: The only lost fact (g9.r1.failure_behavior) is caused by a code bug the agent's own reasoning never touched — it correctly recovered the entire refusal rule (message text, attribute names, 16-token threshold, skip-and-count, EncodingError/ValueError subclassing) from remarks, but never clamped retained_prompt_tokens at 0, so the refusal fires correctly but reports a nonsensical negative value in the TOO_LONG_PAIRS case (line 4894-4901; failing assertion at pointer-sheet line 42-44).

Two wiki-comment carriers (pages 135 and 154) were structurally undiscoverable by the agent's keyword-driven search strategy — neither ever matched a search term it tried — yet both facts they carry (g9.r2.scope, g9.r1.exclusions_or_crossover) still scored 1 because every fact in this run had redundant carriers elsewhere in chat/mail. This is a search-strategy gap that cost nothing only because of the corpus's built-in redundancy (line 4128-4136 for the search attempt; g9.r2.l8/g9.r1.l-fw-2 rows above).

#viewer channel (holding g9.r2.l9, the only remark there) was never dumped — the agent's channel loop only covered engineering, code-review, releases, cookbooks, pipeline (line 2947). Again cost nothing due to redundancy.

All 5 herrings were correctly identified and reversed in the shipped code — the agent explicitly cross-referenced 'Jan 21 version superseded by Apr 24 rule' (line 3031) and 'per p149 Jun 17 comment superseding May 28' (line 4060), showing genuine chronological reasoning rather than picking the first match.
